Class GenerationClassLoader

java.lang.Object
java.lang.ClassLoader
java.security.SecureClassLoader
java.net.URLClassLoader
io.micronaut.dev.loader.GenerationClassLoader
All Implemented Interfaces:
Closeable, AutoCloseable
public final class GenerationClassLoader extends URLClassLoader
One generation of the reloadable tier: a URLClassLoader over a snapshot of the class and resource directories, taken when the generation is created.

The snapshot is what makes a generation immutable: the build output keeps changing underneath a running generation, by the next compilation or by the build tool, and a class the generation resolves lazily must be the one that was there when the generation started, not a newer one that would mix two compilations in one loader. The snapshot is deleted when the generation is closed or collected.

Since:
5.3.0
Author:
graemerocher

    • classFileLock

      public Lock classFileLock()
      The lock a change of the snapshot's class files holds from the first file it writes until it is applied or rolled back: no class loads through the generation meanwhile, so that none is defined from a file the change restores. A load in progress when it is taken finishes first, and a load that waited for it reads the files the change left. The holder may load classes itself, as the JVM does when it verifies a redefinition.
      Returns:
      The lock
      Since:
      5.3.0

    • findResources

      public Enumeration<URL> findResources(String name) throws IOException
      The resources of a name, without the build output's copies of those a live directory holds: a resource the build copied from a resource root would be found twice, which configuration loading rejects as a duplicate, and the copy may be stale. Resources under META-INF/ are left alone: a processor generates those into the class output beside the ones a resource root holds, as service descriptors, and every one counts.

      findResources in class URLClassLoader

    • findResource

      public @Nullable URL findResource(String name)
      The resource of a name, from a live directory first. A resource that belongs to a live directory and is absent from it, deleted by the developer, is not found: the build output's copy of it is stale. Resources under META-INF/ are left alone, as in findResources(String).
